region.text: Jiangdong: Cliopatria's Eastern Wu shape of 207, the lands southeast of the Yangtze

ledger.note: 207: Sun Quan's Jiangdong is Cliopatria's Eastern Wu row. The page gives 200: 'the 18-year-old Sun Quan inherited the lands southeast of the Yangtze River from his brother', and Sun Ce's conquests ran 194-199 (Eastern Wu page); the sibling sun-ce dossier carries the land to 206. 207 is Cliopatria's year, not a page's.

ledger.note: 208: Huang Zu is beaten. The page dates 'Huang Zu's defeat to early 208'; Huang Zu held Jiangxia for Liu Biao. The extent is my reading (Xiakou and the Han mouth).

ledger.note: 210: Jiaozhi submits to Wu. 'After Zhou Yu died in 210, Sun won over the warlords of Jiao Province and appointed Bu Zhi as inspector. Shi Xie submitted to Bu Zhi.' (Shi Xie page: Bu Zhi's appointment dated by a footnote to 210.) Shi Xie ruled Jiaozhi 'for a total of 40 years'.
211: Sun Quan 'moved headquarters from Dantu to Moling in 211 and renamed the city Jianye in 212'.

ledger.note: 215: the Xiang River partition. 'Liu Bei and Sun Quan settle on the Xiang River as their border.' Which commanderies went to Sun Quan is not on the page; Changsha and Guiyang, on the east, are my reading.

region.text: Jing Province's south, 'roughly modern Hunan and parts of Hubei'

ledger.note: 219: Lü Meng takes Jing. 'In 219 Sun Quan broke with Liu Bei and sent Lü Meng to invade Liu's Jing Province holdings. Guan Yu was captured and executed.' (Three Kingdoms page: 'Sun Quan takes the territory east of the Yangtze Gorges'.) The alliance with Shu ends.

region.text: Yiling and the Yangtze Gorges, where Xiaoting was fought

ledger.note: 221: Shu invades Wu to avenge Guan Yu. (The Shu Han page dates the campaign to 222.)
221: Sun Quan becomes King of Wu under Wei. 'On 23 September 221, Cao Pi appointed Sun Quan King of Wu.' (The Eastern Wu page gives 220.) Wu is nominally Wei's vassal until November 222.

region.text: Yiling and the Yangtze Gorges, where Xiaoting was fought

ledger.note: 222: Xiaoting. 'Lu Xun's fire attacks at Xiaoting force Liu Bei to retreat.' Jing stays Wu's.
222: the capital is Wuchang (infobox: Wuchang 222-229). The Sun Quan page names the 229 move to Jianye but not a move to Wuchang.

region.text: the Wei-Wu frontier from Jiangling to the lower Yangtze and the Huai

ledger.note: 222: Wei attacks Wu. 'Wei engaged Wu in a series of armed conflicts throughout the 220s and 230s'; Dongkou (222-223), Jiangling (223), Shiting (228). The frontier is a band of the two Cliopatria shapes of 224.

222: Sun Quan declares Wu independent of Wei. 'In November 222, Sun declared independence by changing the era name' after refusing Cao Pi's demand for a hostage; he keeps the title King of Wu until 229 (Eastern Wu page; infobox 'Independence from Cao Wei: 222').

ledger.note: 227: Shi Hui resists the division of Jiao. Shi Xie died in 226 and Shi Hui succeeded under Wu; Sun Quan made Dai Liang and Lü Dai Inspectors of Jiao and Guang, and 'in 227, when Shi Hui learnt about the new arrangements, he refused to comply'.

notes:
CLIOPATRIA ROWS. Eastern Wu has four shapes (207-237, 238-262, 263-269, 270-282). Wikidata Q274488 is shared with the Spring and Autumn state of Wu (slug wu): a Wikidata mislink, different states; not merged. The row is drawn too late and too small in 207-237: Cliopatria adds Hunan, Hubei, Guangdong, Guangxi and Tonkin only from 238, taking them from its residual Han Dynasty row (3,115 of the 3,117 cells; the han-dynasty dossier drops that row). The new keyframes 209 (Jiangling), 215 (east Hunan), 219 (Jing), 227 (Jiao and Guang) carry the steps the pages date.
START. 207 follows Cliopatria and the sibling sun-ce dossier (195-206, handing over to this row); the pages say Sun Quan inherited in 200 and became King of Wu in 221 and emperor in 229. The found event is therefore confidence 1.
END. Cliopatria keeps Wu to 282; the pages end it in April-May 280 (1 May on the Conquest page, 31 May on the Eastern Wu infobox: a disagreement the page-reader should settle).
DISAGREEMENTS. (1) Sun Quan's King of Wu title: 23 September 221 (Sun Quan page) against 220 (Eastern Wu page). (2) Lü Dai's defeat of Shi Hui: 227 (Shi Xie page) against 226 (Sun Quan page). (3) Xiaoting: 221 (Three Kingdoms) or 222 (Shu Han). (4) The Jing Province split after Red Cliffs: this dossier follows the Three Kingdoms page (Liu Bei takes the Xiang commanderies, Zhou Yu takes Jiangling, 215 Xiang border); the sibling liu-biao dossier, from a page not opened here, gives Changsha, Guiyang and Jiangxia to Sun Quan in 209.
GAPS (page silent). No infobox area on the Eastern Wu page, so the area check could not be made (the Jin 280 infobox figure of 3.1 M km2 for the whole empire is the only comparison). The Linyi (Champa) frontier in Rinan: Cliopatria's Champa row (207-1652) starts in 207, its neighbour list shows contact with Wu from 238; no page opened covers it. The Shanyue campaigns (206, 224-225) are internal; the Yizhou expedition (230-231) and the Liaodong embassies (232-238) moved no border.
COUNTERPARTS WITHOUT A DOSSIER. Shi Xie's Jiaozhi (187-227, vassal of Wu from 210) and the revolt of Lady Triệu (248) have none; propose slug shi-xie.
